newsitem.title: USA: TI to roll out new chips in 2nd half 1997.
newsitem.headline: TI to roll out new chips in 2nd half 1997.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said it will begin volume production of its new high-speed digital signal processor chip in the second half of 1997 with initial volume in the hundreds of thousands of units.

"We'll be in the production phase in the second half of the year and we expect to start up with hundreds of thousands of units," said John Scarisbrick, senior vice president at Texas Instruments' Semiconductor Group.
"We'd be surprised if we weren't producing millions of units by the end of the decade, perhaps tens of millions," he told Reuters.
The Dallas-based semiconductor giant earlier introduced its so-called C6x chip, which can process 1.6 billion instructions per second and is now sampling in limited quantities.
Scarisbrick said the C6x chip is 120 times faster than comparable digital signal processors currently being used in modems.
The new DSP chip is designed for use in emerging communications technologies such as cable modems or digital subscriber line systems.
Such systems can send million of bits of information a second via cable modems over coaxial cable TV wires or over standard copper phone lines in the case of DSL.
These rates are far faster than current modems operating at speeds up to roughly 33,000 bits per second.
